title: Containerization & Orchestration: Docker & Kubernetes
description: Docker package applications into isolated containers. Kubernetes automates container deployment, scaling, load balancing, and self-healing.
detailedExplanation: Docker uses Linux namespaces and cgroups to isolate process resources in light weight images. Kubernetes manages clusters of worker nodes running Pods (containers), controlled by Deployments, Services (kube-proxy), and Ingress controllers.
architectureFlow: Dockerfile -> Docker Build -> Image Registry (ECR/DockerHub) -> Kubernetes Deployment -> ReplicaSet -> Pods -> Ingress / LoadBalancer -> Client
examples: Multi-stage Dockerfile for Node.js production builds
Kubernetes Deployment & HPA (Horizontal Pod Autoscaler) manifest
Docker Compose multi-container setup (Web + Node Server + Redis + Postgres)

interviewQuestions.question: Difference between a Docker Image and a Docker Container?
interviewQuestions.answer: A Docker Image is a read-only immutable template containing application code, runtime, and dependencies. A Docker Container is a runnable instance of a Docker image executing in isolation.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a Kubernetes Pod?
interviewQuestions.answer: A Pod is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes. It wraps one or more containers that share network IP, storage volumes, and runtime specification.

sampleCode:
# Production Multi-Stage Dockerfile for Node.js
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --legacy-peer-deps
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=builder /app/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
EXPOSE 3001
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
bestPractices: Use multi-stage Docker builds to minimize final container image size (<100MB)
Never run containers as root user — use unprivileged non-root users
Define resource limits (CPU/Memory) on all Kubernetes Pod specifications
commonMistakes: Storing API keys or secrets inside static Dockerfile images
Using 'latest' tag in production manifests instead of specific version hashes

title: Cloud Infrastructure & CI/CD Pipelines (AWS, GCP, Azure, GitHub Actions)
description: Cloud hosting services (AWS, Azure, GCP) and automated Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines.
detailedExplanation: CI/CD automates code testing, linting, building, and deployment upon code push (git push). Cloud platforms provide virtual infrastructure like compute (EC2/ECS), storage (S3), CDN edge distribution (CloudFront), and managed databases (RDS).
architectureFlow: Git Commit -> GitHub Push -> GitHub Action Trigger -> Run Tests -> Docker Build -> Push to ECR -> AWS ECS Task Deployment
examples: GitHub Actions workflow for automated testing and Vite deployment to S3 + CloudFront
Terraform Infrastructure as Code (IaC) provisioning AWS VPC and EKS cluster

interviewQuestions.question: What is CI/CD and why is it essential in modern DevOps?
interviewQuestions.answer: Continuous Integration (CI) automatically builds and tests code on every push to detect bugs early. Continuous Deployment (CD) automatically releases passing builds to production environments, enabling zero-downtime shipping.

sampleCode:
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml
name: Build & Deploy
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 20 }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npm test
bestPractices: Use Infrastructure as Code (Terraform / CloudFormation) instead of manual dashboard clicks
Secure CI/CD pipelines using OIDC role assumption rather than static long-lived AWS keys
commonMistakes: Hardcoding IAM access keys in public GitHub repositories
